Learning to Read Across Single-Cell Atlases

Wei Zhang, Na Li

Abstract

We study representation transfer across single-cell atlases from several tissues.

1 Introduction

Understanding cell states across tissues is a central problem in computational biology.

2 Methods

We trained a graph neural network on 12,000 single-cell profiles using a contrastive objective.

The encoder uses a two-layer message-passing network and a batch-correction layer.

2.1 Evaluation

We evaluated the model with five-fold cross-validation across three tissues.

3 Results

The model achieved an AUROC of 0.91 on the held-out cohort, outperforming the baseline by 6 points.

4 Discussion

Our results show that transfer improves rare-cell detection in held-out tissues.

4.1 Limitations

A limitation of this work is that only three tissues were profiled, so generalization to other organs remains untested.

References

Methods for single-cell analysis. Nature 2020.
